reviews.comment: He is a knowledgeable guy but not a great at teaching if you have a picky TA good luck mine was very nitpicky in my section. The biggest issue I had was vague instructions and Assignments constantly being changed after being posted and get ready for AI rants. Good luck with the group project it isn't hard just time consuming. Also grading is slow
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If you've taken COSC 153 with Professor Cooke, you know the drill. His lectures don't accomplish much, so you learn the most in lab with the other professors who are there to help. This class seems daunting, but assignments are graded pretty lightly. There is no reason to get below a B in this class. Weekly pop quizzes, can be in lecture or lab.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Seems like a lot of his assignments are simply just made from bad AI prompts; They don't really make sense and you have to ask questions constantly to clarify. Very nice though. Quizzes are hard but you can still get an A while having a terrible quiz average. HW is pretty easy

He isn't out to try and make you fail, but some things are a bit more complicated than they need to be. A lot of assignments have contradicting instructions but it's basically the same stuff every week so after a few weeks you'll get used to how it is done. You have a group project at the end and if that goes good your grade gets a good boost.

Guy Cooke is a great professor. Some of the ratings here say that he's a great guy but he can't teach, which isn't true. He is very passionate about construction, and it is very apparent in his lectures. The assignment instructions can be unclear at times but you'll be fine. Field trip was fun and the weekly guest speakers are very informative.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Cooke is a great person, but an awful teacher. Nothing covered in the lectures will appear on the pop quizzes or exams, and the expectations for assignments are never clear. There's a huge emphasis on the group project, but you won't know what you're doing for that either. The class isn't too difficult, and the speakers are good.

Reads off slides but sometimes gives exam hints. Guest speakers give good industry insight. Assignment instructions were very unclear and frustrating. Lots of group work and weekly pop quizzes. Grading was inconsistent between him and the TA. He knows his stuff, but the class felt very disorganized.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Gives poor directions and asks questions that can be interpreted several different ways but only wants one answer.

Guy knows what he's talking about, but doesn't teach well. Tons of pop quizzes, midterm, and final, as well as a semester long group project that wasn't that difficult if you get a good group. If you need his help email him, talking to him multiple times after class doesn't matter if he doesn't have an "email" about the problem.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Inconsistent grading between the multiple TA's and professors. Assignments feel like busy work all semester and professor does not seem to have a good grasp on the concept. All TA's and professors give different answers to the same question.

Was scared this semester because of the previous reviews, absolutely amazing professor. I honestly coasted this semester in his class and he brings in the coolest speakers from all the industries. He gives out quizzes which honestly as long as you listen in his class you'll be fine. I never took notes and I was chillin. I'm telling you it's not bad

All of Guy's ratings should be 5 stars, amazing professor with an abundance of experience with Tellepsen. Always ready to help and works extremely hard to bring great guest speakers from all industries to immerse you. Great Guy literally and even better teacher. P.S. his end of year project boosts your grade hugely so don't stress.

Guy Cooke is an awesome professor who gets better every semester. He takes feedback seriously and wants his students to succeed not only in his class but also in their careers. Quizzes are tough, but if you do all the assignments and get a good grade on the project, then you'll have an A, no problem.

Hey, I have a great idea, let's have 2 professors teach the same class where they switch off days, but they aren't on the same page at all. They give conflicting information that contradicts one another. Hey, guess what, they also do not answer their emails lol. You'll pass the class but golly does it make me wanna smash my head into a table

reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class is highly valuable to all future construction professionals. Guy and T.A. Mili are always available to help. Guy refers to his time at Tellepsen often and it is certain helpful when explaining certain concepts. Recommend him any day for Planning and Scheduling (475).

Do not let the poor ratings scare you. He is actually not bad at all and his class is so easy. He grades easy and actually cares about you doing well in the class. He gives an unreal amount of extra credit so its almsot impossible to do bad. If you are at like an 80-84 the entire time in his class with all the extra credit you will make an A.

Professor Cooke also took a little warming up. His tests and quizzes can be confusing at times, and he loves to talk about his past projects, but if you can look past that, he is one of the best professors I've ever had. If you take the time to get to know him, he is a very nice man who cares about your success and does his best to help you succeed
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class is supposed to introduce the Modern Construction Industry and management(He does not do this). His experience is outdated, no teaching skills, can't even make a test or quiz that makes sense. Lectures are pointless. If you are interested in learning about his mediocre golf game and not construction then maybe this is for you.

People give this professor a hard time for fair reason. Exams are confusing and so are quizzes. Directions on at home assignments are constructed using AI which provides a lot of room for questions. Then again, Guy provides numerous opportunities to bring your grade up by a whole letter grade. Do not fear his rating!

Nice guy with the best of intentions, but I never understood his lectures at all. It seemed that the tests and quizzes never matched what he was teaching, which made it very hard. This class was much harder than an intro class should be and had me wondering if I had chosen the wrong major.

Where do I begin? Multiple errors on tests, changed the syllabus multiple times throughout the year. Likes to rattle on and talk about the good old days. This is an intro class, no one should have to fight to get a B or a low A. The material is easy if you just read straight out of the textbook. Lectures are incoherent. Good f'n luck.

Professor Cooke hasn't taught in 20 years, so he is super knowledgeable but needs to help in the teaching aspect. I think with more practice at creating assignments and tests, his teaching methods in the future will be better for future classes. Overall, he is tough but you will learn a few things.

Lectures are uninformative: Talks about his golf game and spends way to much time on things that do not apply to the class. The textbook houses all of the material, making the lectures pointless, and he gets the info from the textbook wrong on tests and quizzes. His standards for grading are Ineffective and hard to understand for students. Avoid!
If you study the book, you will be fine. The lectures do not help because he never talks about construction.

Doesn't teach. Lectures consist of golf and stories of projects from 20 years ago. Lectures are irrelevant. You'll do equally as well on the tests/quizzes if you stay home or attend class. Every test/quiz has a failing class average. Difficult class--nobody knows what homework/quizzes questions are asking. You are set up for failure. Please avoid!

Professor Cooke is a very nice guy but a horrible teacher. He talks about everything but construction and on the rare occasion he does, he talks about a project he worked on 20 years ago. All of his slides are 20 years old and are outdated. The information on his slides also contradict the information in the textbook and his tests are T/F and SATA.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Maybe used to be able to teach, not anymore. Changes syllabus every 2 days. Does not lecture about any materiel on test or quizzes. Hates when you ask questions about the assignments that have no instruction. Makes the TA take on all of his work.  I hope that he will not be teaching next year. DO NOT TAKE THIS MAN FOR COSC 153...
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Cooke is a nice guy but a TERRIBLE professor. He does not teach anything in class. His quizzes have stuff that he has never taught in class, he expects us to teach ourselves everything and get all our info from the textbook for the quizzes. The class avg was failing for the 1st quiz which is concerning since this should be the easiest COSC course.

Guy Cooke obviously is passionate about construction, but his lectures do not relate to the class very much. His assignments almost never have clear instructions and he became so frustrated that we did not understand he ended class early after telling us to change our major if we didn't understand.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The dude is so awesome he is very passionate about his job and loves to talk in class to the students. he also brings a speaker to the class to further explain the construction industry.

Cooke would rather talk about his round of golf than give a coherent lecture. He hasn't taught in 20-plus years and it shows. Become upset when you ask for clarification, is baffled if you don't get it right off the bat. Get ready to be lost.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy
